chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud from Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Sufyan, who said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Hamdan al-Mad'ani narrated to us from Ziyad al-Qandi, who said: Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) said:

"I love for you what I love for myself, and I dislike for you what I dislike for myself. Perfect the prayer in the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), and at the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and in Kufa."

key_terms.أُحِبُّ لَكَ مَا أُحِبُّهُ لِنَفْسِي: I love for you what I love for myself (a key ethical maxim)
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two Sanctuaries, referring to Mecca and Medina
key_terms.الْكُوفَةِ: Kufa, a major city in Iraq with significant Shia historical importance

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kazim advise regarding prayer locations and ethical conduct?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) extends the ethical principle of 'wishing for others what you wish for yourself' to specific acts of worship, emphasizing the spiritual merit of perfecting Salah in the two major sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), the shrine of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and Kufa. This narration highlights the Shia emphasis on the sanctity of specific geographical sites as loci of divine connection, linking the Prophet's family's legacy to communal prayer practices.
